connector: What did you eat today? Long ago, the answer depended on who you were. Today’s article shows two sides: the rich and the poor. Look for the words that split them apart.

a.raw: at the great feast lord neville served roast swan
a.fixed: At the great feast, Lord Neville served roast swan.
a.why: At starts the sentence, so it gets a capital A. A comma comes after the opening part. Lord is a title right before his name, Neville. A period ends the sentence.

b.raw: in the kitchens of dover castle the cooks baked pies
b.fixed: In the kitchens of Dover Castle, the cooks baked pies.
b.why: In starts the sentence. Dover Castle is the name of one place, so both words get capitals. A comma comes after the opening part. A period ends the sentence.

cards.title: Job Spotlight: The Castle Cook
cards.sub: A real job in the Middle Ages
cards.todo: Read about this real job. Then read the two questions and the article.
text: A big castle kitchen had a head cook and many helpers.
They baked bread, stirred pottage, and roasted meat over a huge open fire.
A kitchen boy sometimes had a hot job: turning the meat on a long spit, around and around, for hours.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. What did you eat today? Long ago, the answer depended on who you were. Today’s article shows two sides, the rich and the poor.
transcripts.guide1: Word study review. Roll trans words, hunt for capital-letter mistakes, and roll VCCV words.
transcripts.guide2: Read about medieval food. Look for the words that split the rich from the poor.
transcripts.guide3: Today you start writing: your topic sentence and one detail.

notes.wordParts: The word part trans means across. transport = to carry across. translate = to carry words across into another language. Some words only start with t r a n, like tranquil (calm).
notes.grammar: Capital letters start every sentence and every important word in a name: people (Queen Eleanor), places (Tower of London) and titles. Small words like the, of and in stay small inside a name or title, unless they come first.
notes.spelling: VCCV means vowel, consonant, consonant, vowel. Split the word between the two consonants: bas · ket, tun · nel. Letters like ph and th stay together.
notes.wgrd: Some articles show two sides. Words like most and very differently tell you the author is switching sides.

virtue.name: diligence
virtue.title: Diligence Watch: Is someone working hard?

items.t: People grew their own food in gardens or small farm plots.
items.why: Growing food takes work every day, all season long.

items.t: A king's feast might include roasted meat, pies, fish, fruits, and sweet pastries.
items.why: That tells what was on the table, not who worked to make it.

items.t: Meat was a rare treat for most ordinary people.
items.why: That is a fact about food, not about someone working.
